content: Ibn Turka never names Akhlāṭī in his writings but calls him 'our Sayyid' (sayyid-i mā, R. Shaqq-i Qamar 116), 'the Sayyidic Presence' (R. Ḥurūf f. 156b; R. Arbaʿīniyya f. 120b, both MS Majlis 10196) and 'the sublime Sayyidic Threshold' (K. al-Mafāḥiṣ, preface, f. 52b). Melvin-Koushki takes this as an index of unparalleled regard.
refers_to_primary: Ibn Turka, R. Shaqq-i Qamar 116; R. Ḥurūf f. 156b; K. al-Mafāḥiṣ preface f. 52b
